{{DISPLAYTITLE:Janko group J<sub>2</sub>}}
{{Group theory sidebar |Finite}}

In the area of modern algebra known as [[group theory]], the '''Janko group''' ''J<sub>2</sub>'' or the '''Hall-Janko group''' ''HJ''  is a [[sporadic simple group]] of [[Order (group theory)|order]]
:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;604,800 = 2<sup>7</sup>{{·}}3<sup>3</sup>{{·}}5<sup>2</sup>{{·}}7
: ≈ 6{{e|5}}.

==History and properties==
''J<sub>2</sub>'' is one of the 26 [[Sporadic group]]s and is also called '''Hall–Janko–Wales group'''.  In 1969 [[Zvonimir Janko]] predicted J<sub>2</sub> as one of two new simple groups having 2<sup>1+4</sup>:A<sub>5</sub> as a centralizer of an involution (the other is the [[Janko group J3]]). It was constructed by {{harvs|txt |authorlink=Marshall Hall (mathematician) |first1=Marshall|last1=Hall |first2=David|last2=Wales |year=1968}} as a [[rank 3 permutation group]] on 100 points.

Both the [[Schur multiplier]] and the [[outer automorphism group]] have order 2. As a permutation group on 100 points J<sub>2</sub> has [[involution (mathematics)#group theory|involutions]] moving all 100 points and involutions moving just 80 points. The former involutions are 
products of 25 double transportions, an odd number, and hence lift to 4-elements in the [[Covering_groups_of_the_alternating_and_symmetric_groups|double cover]] 2.A<sub>100</sub>. The double cover 2.J<sub>2</sub> occurs as a [[Conway_group#Suzuki_chain_of_product_groups|subgroup]] of the Conway group Co<sub>0</sub>.

J<sub>2</sub> is the only one of the 4 Janko groups that is a [[subquotient]] of the [[monster group]]; it is thus part of what [[Robert Griess]] calls the Happy Family. Since it is also found in the [[Conway group Co1]], it is therefore part of the second generation of the Happy Family.

== Representations ==
It is a subgroup of [[Index of a subgroup|index]] two of the group of automorphisms of the [[Hall–Janko graph]], leading to a [[permutation representation]] of degree 100. It is also a subgroup of index two of the group of automorphisms of the Hall–Janko [[Near Polygon|Near Octagon]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.win.tue.nl/~aeb/graphs/HJ315.html|title = The near octagon on 315 points}}</ref> leading to a permutation representation of degree 315.

It has a [[modular representation]] of dimension six over the field of four elements; if in [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] two we have {{nowrap|''w''<sup>2</sup> + ''w'' + 1 {{=}} 0}}, then J<sub>2</sub> is generated by the two matrices

:<math>
{\mathbf A} = \begin{pmatrix}
w^2 & w^2 &   0 &   0 &   0 & 0 \\ 
  1 & w^2 &   0 &   0 &   0 & 0 \\ 
  1 &   1 & w^2 & w^2 &   0 & 0 \\ 
  w &   1 &   1 & w^2 &   0 & 0 \\ 
  0 & w^2 & w^2 & w^2 &   0 & w \\ 
w^2 &   1 & w^2 &   0 & w^2 & 0
\end{pmatrix}
</math>

and

:<math>
{\mathbf B} = \begin{pmatrix}
  w & 1 & w^2 &   1 & w^2 & w^2 \\ 
  w & 1 &   w &   1 &   1 & w \\ 
  w & w & w^2 & w^2 &   1 & 0 \\ 
  0 & 0 &   0 &   0 &   1 & 1 \\ 
w^2 & 1 & w^2 & w^2 &   w & w^2 \\ 
w^2 & 1 & w^2 &   w & w^2 & w
\end{pmatrix}.
</math>

These matrices satisfy the equations

:<math>
{\mathbf A}^2 = {\mathbf B}^3 = ({\mathbf A}{\mathbf B})^7 = 
({\mathbf A}{\mathbf B}{\mathbf A}{\mathbf B}{\mathbf B})^{12} = 1.
</math>

(Note that matrix multiplication on a finite field of order 4 is defined slightly differently from ordinary matrix multiplication. See {{section link|Finite field|Field with four elements}} for the specific addition and multiplication tables, with ''w'' the same as ''a'' and ''w''{{sup|2}} the same as ''1 + a''.)

J<sub>2</sub> is thus a [[Hurwitz group]], a finite homomorphic image of the [[(2,3,7) triangle group]].

The matrix representation given above constitutes an embedding into [[Leonard Eugene Dickson|Dickson's]] group [[Group of Lie type|''G''<sub>2</sub>(4)]]. There is only one conjugacy class of J<sub>2</sub> in ''G''<sub>2</sub>(4). Every subgroup J<sub>2</sub> contained in ''G''<sub>2</sub>(4) extends to a subgroup J<sub>2</sub>:2{{nbsp}}= Aut(J<sub>2</sub>) in ''G''<sub>2</sub>(4):2{{nbsp}}= Aut(''G''<sub>2</sub>(4)) (''G''<sub>2</sub>(4) extended by the field automorphisms of '''F'''<sub>4</sub>). ''G''<sub>2</sub>(4) is in turn isomorphic to a subgroup of the [[Conway group]] Co<sub>1</sub>.
